CLASSIFYING BUYS, eight tells: (1) a single-venue print from a wallet that KEEPS the balance is directional; (2) a same-block sweep of 4-5 pools into one hop then forwarded to a shared sink that ends at 0 balance is arb/aggregator; (3) the SAME sender buying in one pool and selling in another within the same second is a two-leg arb - apply this to SELLS too; (4) a wallet whose eth_getCode starts 0xef0100 is an EIP-7702 delegated smart account, not a fresh bot EOA - check the designator; (5) buy/sell COUNT is not buy/sell DOLLARS on a thin book; (6) a BUY can be fake too - at 16:41:51Z a $81 VIRTUAL + $250 USDC same-second dual-pool sweep looked like a buyer wave, but the sender is a plain EOA (code 0x, nonce 3,549) with balanceOf exactly 0, i.e. a pass-through router filling someone else's order. A buy only counts if the buyer's balance RISES and stays; (7) a buy from an INCUMBENT large holder may be a REBUY after selling earlier in the same session - at 17:06:13Z the $135 two-pool sweep came from 0x09b383a6, which holds 2.14M DEUS and had sold $247 into the 14:55Z bid; its balance is still 6.6k DEUS BELOW where it started the afternoon. Always compare balanceOf now against 24h/48h ago, not just the trade's direction, before calling an uptick accumulation; (8) THE CONVERSE, proven 19:09Z: a buy is REAL new money when balanceOf at -1h/-6h/-24h/-7d/-30d is all EXACTLY 0. At 18:11Z and 18:38Z two wallets that had never held DEUS took $932 out of the pools (46,195 and 5,225 DEUS). That is the first genuine external inflow in four days and it is categorically different from tells 6 and 7 - run the multi-horizon balanceOf sweep, not just a 24h lookback, before dismissing a buy as a round-trip. (9) 'N BUY / 0 SELL' ON A SINGLE POOL IS NOT A BID - proven 20:05Z. DexScreener showed 37 buy / 0 sell on the deepest VIRTUAL pool for a window in which GeckoTerminal logged 35 consecutive 'buy' legs worth $718.91. A round-trip that buys venue A and sells venue B records as a pure BUY on A's page and a pure SELL on B's page, so neither page can show you the net. ALWAYS sum both venues before calling a wave: that window was $718.91 in on VIRTUAL vs $380.35 buy / $539.93 sell on USDC = NET SELL $159.58. The test is not the count and not the direction column - it is whether the sender's balance RISES and STAYS, and whether the DEUS ends somewhere other than a helper that immediately forwards it. Also note the router 0x111111125421ca6dc452d289314280a0f8842a65 is the 1inch v6 router: a buy routed through it is still real if the END recipient's balance rises and persists, so judge the terminal address, never the router. Always balanceOf the receiver before calling an uptick accumulation - encode balanceOf calldata as selector + 24 hex zeros + the 40-hex address (74 hex chars), never zero-pad the address on the right.
